UPDATED 10:00 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026
INFRA
With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia’s CUDA moat in its crosshairs
by Mike Wheatley
Luminal AI Inc. has outlined a plan to tear down Nvidia Corp.’s formidable software moat in the artificial intelligence chip industry after raising $23 million in early-stage funding.
Today’s Series A round was led by Standard Capital and saw participation from existing investors such as Y Combinator, SagaVC, Liquid 2 and Felicis, bringing Luminal’s total amount raised to date to more than $28 million. It comes about a year after the startup raised $5.3 million in seed funding.
Everybody knows about Nvidia these days. The chipmaker has ridden the generative AI wave to a staggering $5 trillion market valuation, surpassing rivals such as Apple Inc., Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. to become the most valuable publicly traded company in the world. But anyone who assumes that it’s solely Nvidia’s graphics processing units that set it apart would be mistaken, for the real reason for its dominance of the AI computing industry is not just silicon, but software.
For almost two decades, Nvidia’s proprietary Compute Unified Device Architecture or CUDA software framework has been the real differentiator, serving as a virtually impenetrable barrier that prevents rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Google LLC and Amazon Web Services Inc. from stripping away its market lead. Though those rivals have developed some very powerful GPUs and custom application-specific integrated circuits for running AI workloads at lower costs than Nvidia’s hardware, they haven’t been able to match the scale of Nvidia’s software ecosystem.
Virtually every major AI framework, including TensorFlow and PyTorch, has been built natively on Nvidia’s CUDA software, enabling developers to run their AI models on Nvidia’s GPUs without any modifications. But to run their models on alternative chips, developers need to rewrite much of the underlying code, which is challenging and time-consuming work. That’s why the vast majority of AI workloads still run on Nvidia’s chips.
Many developers don’t want to be paying the exorbitant fees needed to rent Nvidia’s GPUs or purchase them outright, but they also don’t want to spend months at a time fine-tuning their codebases to get their AI models to run optimally on alternative hardware, and it’s this challenge that Luminal intends to solve for them.
The startup’s solution is a two-pronged architecture platform that consists of its proprietary search compiler and a fully managed inference cloud that combine to eliminate the hassles of bringing AI workloads onto different chips.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Joe Fioti told SiliconANGLE that the compiler works by systematically exploring different ways of running neural networks on the target chip in order to come up with the most optimal path. It benchmarks each variation until it finds the best possible solution, and then it automatically generates the code developers need.
Once the code is ready, it caches the implementation so it can be reused across recurring inference workloads. In this way, it allows developers to run their AI applications across heterogeneous chip architectures with minimal fuss, Fioti said.
“We started out building in the open on GitHub as AI adoption took off, and quickly saw how much demand there was for a more efficient way to run AI models across different hardware,” Fioti said of the company’s origins.
Luminal’s compiler and inference cloud are designed primarily for running high-throughput, continuous-uptime AI applications that demand massively scalable inference. Think applications such as AI coding tools, automated image generation engines, AI video generators and real-time voice agents.
“The cost of running AI shouldn’t limit who gets to build it,” Fioti said. “We’re building the infrastructure to make high-performance inference more accessible, giving developers more choice beyond Nvidia’s ecosystem without forcing them to compromise on speed or cost.”
Luminal launched its compiler and public cloud-based inference infrastructure just four months ago and adoption is growing rapidly. It’s already processing more than 45 trillion tokens per month – a number that’s roughly equivalent to 10% of the total tokens consumed so far by Together AI Inc., an $8 billion-valued infrastructure unicorn that has been serving the market for more than four years already. The startup has established a strong partnership with AWS, and runs a significant amount of its workloads on that company’s Tranium processors.
Going forward, Luminal’s plans include expanding its engineering team, scaling its go-to-market operations and optimizing its compiler and inference infrastructure to support more chip hardware and AI models.
Standard Capital’s Dalton Caldwell said he’s betting on Luminal because AI inference is the fastest-growing market in the world. “We backed it because of its deep technical expertise and its demonstrated proof that it can squeeze fantastic performance out of heterogeneous hardware,” he said. “Luminal’s ability to get the most out of GPUs that have already been purchased … is incredibly high leverage.”
Though Luminal has had a promising start, it’s certainly not the only company trying to break Nvidia’s CUDA stranglehold on the AI industry. Both Google and AWS have their own things going on, notably launching alternative AI frameworks to PyTorch that make it easier for developers to create AI models and applications that can run on their native processors.
Luminal also faces competition from startups such as Spectral Compute Ltd. , which offers a programming toolkit and compiler that enables CUDA-based code to run natively on any AI-accelerated chip. There are also open-source efforts such as the UXL Foundation’s OneAPI , which converts CUDA code into software that can easily run on any silicon.

11 Ноя, 2026
Американский стартап привлёк $20 млн на космические аппараты, которые сами собираются на орбите
Новости
Rendezvous Robotics
28 октября стартап Rendezvous Robotics из Голдена в штате Колорадо объявил о посевном раунде на $20 млн. Его возглавили венчурные компании MaC Venture Capital и Toyota Ventures, а средства пойдут на разработку нового поколения аппаратов, лётные демонстрации и расширение команды.
Помимо лидеров, в раунде участвовали фонд University of Michigan Endowment, Astera, Industrious Ventures, Humbition и NextView Ventures. Компанию и дальше поддержали существующие инвесторы Aurelia Foundry, ATX Venture Partners и Mana Ventures.
- Advertisement -
Стартап ищет выход из ограничений, которые накладывает запуск. Большинство аппаратов проектируют так, чтобы они поместились в головной обтекатель — защитную оболочку на вершине ракеты, под которой летит груз. Из-за этого ещё до запуска приходится идти на компромиссы в выработке энергии, вычислительных мощностях, размере антенн и теплоотводе, хотя потребность во всём этом растёт.
Гендиректор Джо Лэндон пояснил Payload, что отрасль не хочет аппаратов меньшего размера и меньшей мощности. «Никто не говорит о том, чтобы делать спутники меньше и менее функциональными, — сказал он. — Все хотят больше мощности, больше теплоотвода, более крупные антенны, более чувствительную связь. Но этого не достичь, пока мы не научимся строить прямо в космосе».
Follow Mediasat on Google News : the latest in TV, telecom and tech
Rendezvous Robotics предлагает другой подход — аппарат из компактных независимых модулей-плиток. Их запускают по отдельности, а на орбите они самостоятельно маневрируют, выравниваются и соединяются в одну конструкцию, которую после запуска можно перестроить под новые задачи. Этот подход вырос из почти десятилетних исследований соосновательницы компании Ариэль Экблау в Массачусетском технологическом институте (MIT) в рамках программы TESSERAE. Ранние поколения TESSERAE уже проверяли на суборбитальной ракете New Shepard компании Blue Origin и во время двух миссий на Международной космической станции (МКС).
Сейчас Rendezvous Robotics разрабатывает новое поколение более крупных независимых модулей, а их движение, выравнивание и сборку проверяет на Земле. Эти испытания продолжат серией параболических полётов в ноябре 2026 года, во время которых самолёт ненадолго создаёт невесомость. В этих полётах испытают электромагнитный привод и движение модулей. Отдельно от них, в декабре на МКС, проведут заключительную демонстрацию TESSERAE пятого поколения — 32 плитки должны автономно собраться в трёхмерную конструкцию.
Демонстрационную миссию на низкой околоземной орбите запланировали не ранее апреля 2028 года. В ней семь независимых модулей должны автономно соединиться в один аппарат, разделиться и снова собраться в иной конфигурации без помощи внешних роботизированных манипуляторов. Компания называет её первой в своём роде и уже зарезервировала место в совместном запуске (rideshare), где модули выведут на орбиту вместе с другими грузами.
Модульность даёт и практическую выгоду. Оператор может менять конфигурацию аппарата, добавлять новые модули или заменять неисправные прямо на орбите, а не строить и запускать новый аппарат. По словам Лэндона, нынешнее обслуживание спутников сводится к продлению срока службы, тогда как система Rendezvous при повреждении может сама изменить свою структуру на лучшую из доступных. Лэндон допускает и создание на орбите склада модулей, который будет выдавать запасные части по требованию.

candidates.snippet: Dallas AI Startup 4Minds Raises $15M Series A at $500M Valuation Dallas Innovates
candidates.text:
Dallas-based AI startup 4Minds, which emerged from stealth mode in April, is already halfway to unicorn status. The company said today that it has raised a $15 million Series A round at a $500 million post-money valuation.
Investors include Dallas-based Waterwood Capital Group and Lubbock-based Isom Holdings — both led in part by Clayton Isom, whose family founded Wichita Falls-based oil and gas management company Stephens & Johnson in the 1960s — and several family offices with ties to the energy and data center industries.
The startup plans to use the money to expand its sales and marketing teams. It focuses on selling to companies in financial services, banking, insurance, biotech, pharmaceutical and other regulated industries, as well as consumer packaged goods, retail and logistics. It also will add to its product development team.
A new way to automate enterprise AI
At 4Minds, developers created software to help large companies build AI systems that understand their business. The platform automatically pulls data from more than 40 business systems, scrubs it and organizes it into a “knowledge graph” that maps how the data is related. The knowledge graph then continuously trains the AI models on business uses, ensuring information stays current. It all runs inside a company’s own system, so its sensitive data never touches a public AI model.
It’s “the easiest way for any enterprise to build end-to-end automation for AI workloads,” co-founder and CEO Ryan Trimberger told Dallas Innovates.
The 4Minds team sees enormous potential, Trimberger said. Large companies are ramping up spending on AI. Enterprise AI spending in the U.S. reached an annualized run rate of $177 billion in September 2026, up more than fivefold from $33 billion a year earlier, according to a Menlo Ventures report .
Many companies aren’t realizing the returns they’d like from those investments, though. Factors include difficulty scrubbing data for use in an automated AI system, rising costs and data security concerns, Trimberger said. Tackling all those issues at once is 4Minds’ selling point.
“When we initially started, we were focused on making smaller [large language models] really powerful, and the thesis was around cybersecurity,” Trimberger said. “That’s just native to who we are as a business. … We realized very quickly this wasn’t just cybersecurity. This was going to be every business, every domain, every vertical.”
Building in Deep Ellum
Trimberger founded 4Minds in 2024 along with Jerome Naidoo and Jason Nocco. The three founders make up the first three minds in the company’s name. The fourth represents the company’s customers, Trimberger said.
The team stayed small at the outset, focusing exclusively on product development. As recently as February, 4Minds employed just 13 people. Today, its headcount tops 60. Trimberger said he expects that number to approach 100 by early 2027.
He declined to share the startup’s revenue targets but said, “We think we can scale and be in the nine-figure range very quickly.”
The company sells 4Minds on the AWS and Microsoft marketplaces. It’s also part of AWS’ Global Startup Program and the Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program , and will be featured at this month’s Microsoft Ignite 2026.
Access to strong research universities played a key role in choosing Dallas as the home for 4Minds’ product team, Trimberger said.
The company has recruited several people from the University of North Texas’ data science program and has formed a relationship with Dean Kinshuk, who leads UNT’s newly named Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics. It maintains similar relationships with the University of Texas at Arlington for machine learning and Southern Methodist University for cybersecurity, Trimberger said.
“We’ve been really, really intentional to try to build an ecosystem for not just hiring but for long-term, private-sector research,” he said. “We consider ourselves an AI lab, and I think a lot of that is just an extension of our higher ed partnerships.”
Its entire product team is based in North Texas, working from an office in Deep Ellum, a location that Trimberger said is a great fit.
“We needed something that was going to be modern, cool and fit what we were building,” he said. “I don’t think there’s really anybody doing this kind of frontier-level tech in DFW, so we need a space to reflect that. We are proud to be in Dallas.”
Why family offices?
Because 4Minds concentrates on the software layer of generative AI, it doesn’t need the large investments required by companies with significant infrastructure buildouts , Trimberger said. This allows what he described as an unconventional approach to fundraising, seeking smaller amounts of money from family offices.
“We’re not building infrastructure like a data center company would, so our operating capital is much lighter,” he said. “So, we’ve decided to forgo the traditional venture capital for our Series A and focus exclusively on Dallas-based family offices. That’s a strategic avenue for us.”
The startup’s investors can be a built-in customer base, as they look not just to invest in AI but to introduce AI to portfolio companies, Trimberger said. The approach also means 4Minds’ investors understand what it takes to operate and scale a business.
“These are people who have already built their own successful businesses,” he said. “They’ve built their own empires, so there is an immediate mutual respect there.”
Waterwood Capital’s developers used 4Minds’ technology for months before the firm invested in the company, Waterwood co-founder Clayton Isom said in a statement. The family office’s other portfolio companies include IronHorse Power Services, Evergreen Power Solutions and FairBill Solutions, all based in Dallas; Weatherford-based 3B Inspection; and The Woodlands-based 3B Surveying.

Clawlab Raises Over $15 Million in Pre-A3 Funding to Bring Smart Knitting Home
News provided by

SHENZHEN, China , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clawlab, a technology startup developing smart tools for textile creation, has raised more than $15 million in a Pre-A3 funding round led by miHoYo. Vision Plus Capital and Shunwei Capital also increased their investments through super pro rata participation. The round brings Clawlab's total funding to approximately $25 million across four equity rounds. Its shareholder base includes Sequoia China, Shunwei Capital, YM Capital, Vision Plus Capital, and miHoYo, bringing together leading venture capital firms and a strategic corporate investor.
Investors Back Clawlab's Vision for a New Consumer Category
With AI software commanding much of the market's attention, Clawlab's more than $15 million funding round reflects investor interest in a different opportunity: the untapped consumer potential of smart knitting.
The opportunity comes from a gap between rising consumer demand and the tools available to meet it. Interest in personalized, hands-on creation is growing, yet most knitting equipment remains designed for factories and professional users. Pattern development, stitch control, and machine operation still require specialist expertise. The category lacks a desktop device capable of bringing industrial-grade knitting capabilities within reach of individual creators.
Clawlab is addressing that gap with the world's first smart knitting machine designed for home use. It turns an image or idea into a finished knitted item, handling pattern preparation, stitchwork, and repetitive production while leaving the design, colors, and intended use to the user.
That flexibility supports a wide range of applications, from scarves and doll clothes to pet accessories and personalized gifts. A hobby project can also grow into custom work or a small business. Clawlab is set to unveil this smart knitting machine to a global audience at CES 2027.
The Engineering Foundation Behind Clawlab
Bringing professional knitting equipment into the home involves more than reducing its size. The real challenge is translating complex engineering into a product that feels intuitive to everyday users. Clawlab's founder and CEO Wenxin Hu previously worked as a hardware engineer at DJI and Meituan, while most members of the company's core R&D team are also former DJI employees. Together, they bring experience developing consumer-grade smart hardware and other technically complex products.
That background has shaped Clawlab's approach to product development. Rather than simply miniaturizing existing equipment or adding digital features, the company is rethinking the knitting experience across hardware, software, and interaction design around the needs of individual creators. The technology takes on the complexity, while users retain control of the creative process.
The Long-Term Vision in Knitting
Clawlab chose knitting based on a simple premise: textiles meet one of the most basic and enduring needs of everyday life.
"Textiles meet a broad, long-standing need in everyday life. Standardized products are abundant, but consumers' desire for personal style, customization, and emotional expression remains underserved," said Wenxin Hu. "We want to reconnect ideas, design, and production so that people without professional training can create through knitting."
Their longer-term ambition is to make knitting an everyday medium of expression. Smart knitting equipment, design software, and a creator community can help people turn ideas, memories, and care for others into one-of-a-kind pieces they can hold, share, and pass on.
About Clawlab
Clawlab is a technology startup founded in 2023 that develops smart tools for textile creation. It is building the future of knitting through a combination of innovative knitting technologies and a connected maker community. Its mission, "Push knitting forward. Bring more ideas to life," is to develop the tools and technology that help more people turn what they imagine into something they can hold. Clawlab's vision is to make knitting an everyday language for expression, much like words and pictures, through which people can tell their stories, preserve memories, and connect with others. For more information, please visit www.clawlab.com

SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Delphina , whose Context Factory uses AI agents to build and maintain the business context behind trusted AI analytics, announced $7.5 million in new funding, bringing its total funding to $15 million. The round was co-led by Radical Ventures and Costanoa, with participation from Tenacity Capital joining high-profile angels Fei-Fei Li, Nobel laureate Guido Imbens, and early employees of Anthropic and OpenAI. . Delphina will use the funding to scale the Context Factory and grow its go-to-market and customer engineering teams.
Delphina was built to meet data teams' standards, but business teams now ask 73% of the questions on the platform, and CEOs at more than half of its customers are active users. At Substack, more than 70% of employees use Delphina, including CEO Chris Best. Other customers include LATAM Airlines, Gen Digital, Upstart, Udemy, Medely, Coursera, and BaseCamp Franchising.
"We want to give our people superpowers with AI. Delphina does that for data," said Chris Best, CEO of Substack. "Now our teams get accurate answers in seconds instead of waiting weeks in a queue. It's changed how we make decisions."
AI analytics is only as good as what it knows about the business: which tables are trusted, how metrics are defined, and what experienced analysts know but never wrote down. Most companies build that context by hand, and it goes stale as the business changes. The Context Factory hands that work to agents. They build a working baseline from a company's existing data and documents in hours, find and fix gaps as people ask questions, and route important changes to domain experts for approval.
"At Uber, everyone, including the CEO, was hands-on with data. That direct line to the numbers was a real advantage, but it took an army of data engineers to keep it from collapsing into chaos," said Jeremy Hermann, Delphina's CEO and co-founder. "The Context Factory gives every company that same advantage. Agents do the heavy lifting, and data teams become the knowledge captains who decide how the business sees its numbers."
"Most companies are data-obsessed but struggle to become data-driven," said Duncan Gilchrist, Delphina's President and co-founder. "When everyone can get trusted answers, everyone suddenly has questions. Ops, sales, marketing and finance teams are now the heaviest users of Delphina, and they keep coming back."
Hermann built and led Uber's Michelangelo machine learning platform and co-founded Tecton, which was acquired by Databricks. Gilchrist led global pricing data science at Uber. The Context Factory is available today at delphina.ai .
About Delphina
Delphina gives everyone in a company, from the front line to the CEO, trusted answers from the company's own data. Its Context Factory uses AI agents to build and maintain the business knowledge that enables accurate AI analytics, with experts approving important changes. Delphina is based in San Francisco and backed by Radical Ventures and Costanoa Ventures. Learn more at delphina.ai .

AI-enabled virtual mental health provider Siggy has launched out of stealth with $6 million in pre-seed funding to develop a continuous care platform combining therapy, prescription management and AI-powered patient support. The startup is backed by Village Global and several angel investors.
Siggy aims to deliver personalized mental health care through a system that integrates human clinicians with AI tools for patient intake and support between appointments. Its intake process is free, and patients pay only if they choose to proceed with treatment.
Patients begin with a free, anonymous conversation with Siggy’s AI, without requiring an account or login. The system retains their history, allowing them to avoid repeating information when they consult a provider. An AI-powered preliminary diagnosis is reviewed by clinicians, who then present treatment options.
After an initial call with a human provider, patients can log in to add existing providers or relatives to the system and confirm their treatment goals. Those who accept treatment meet a human clinician monthly and can engage with Siggy’s AI between visits.
The AI therapy agent draws on patients’ full histories to help them work through treatment goals, recall prescribed exercises and discuss their progress. It does not answer medical questions and directs patients to human providers for clinical guidance. Safety protocols are also in place to flag patients with higher-acuity needs to clinicians.
Siggy also connects with wearables and offers a one-minute daily check-in covering sleep, mood, physical well-being, and medication side effects. These inputs contribute to a daily Siggy Score, measured on a scale of 0 to 100 and visible to both patients and clinicians. The platform flags emerging patterns to clinicians, while weekly check-ins during the first two months allow providers to assess whether medication doses should be maintained, increased or changed.
“It can build a really detailed picture of you rather fast, and the idea is if there are behavior patterns that are recurrent…[Siggy can] begin to help people gain agency and recognize them before they happen,” Siggy co-founder and CEO Jonathan Sabbagh told Fierce Healthcare.
Sabbagh co-founded the company with Edvard Engesaeth, M.D., who serves as COO and previously co-founded Nurx. Daniel Montville, M.D., a Mayo Clinic-trained psychiatrist, is the company’s chief medical officer. Sabbagh previously spent two decades in finance before pursuing psychology and co-founding Journey Clinical, a US-based psychedelic-assisted therapy network.
The launch comes amid challenges with continuity in mental health treatment. About 16% of American adults take antidepressants, while one-fifth discontinue treatment before completing the recommended course. Siggy can prescribe medications, excluding controlled substances, and clinicians can oversee medication tapering when patients are ready.
The company is covered by major commercial payers across all 50 states, including Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, UnitedHealthcare and Humana. It also accepts Medicaid, Medicare and TRICARE, and offers its services free to veterans.
In the longer term, Siggy plans to use speech analytics, laboratory results, genetic testing and biomarkers to identify other conditions, including diabetes and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). It also aims to develop neural datasets to support clinical trials for technologies such as brain implants.

ORLANDO, Fla. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Backswing Ventures, the defense venture capital firm, today announced its investment in Vigilant Works , a Ukrainian defense technology company developing autonomous counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS), high-speed interceptor platforms, and radar-based detection capabilities designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Continue Reading
Backswing Ventures logo
The investment will support Vigilant Works' continued development of its autonomous guidance technologies, next-generation radar capabilities, and expansion of its operations as the company prepares to scale production and establish a broader presence across NATO-allied countries.
Backswing Ventures invests selectively in companies addressing critical challenges across defense and national security. As aerial threats continue to evolve in speed, sophistication, and scale, the ability to detect, track, and intercept them autonomously is becoming increasingly important. Vigilant Works is developing an integrated approach to counter-UAS operations, combining high-speed interception, autonomous guidance, and radar technology into a scalable defense ecosystem.
Founded by a team of engineers and defense technology entrepreneurs, Vigilant Works is developing an autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem combining interceptor platforms, proprietary autonomy technologies, and radar-based detection capabilities. Its first-generation Algiz-1 has undergone battlefield testing, providing operational experience that informs the development of its next-generation systems. The company is currently advancing Algiz-2, a next-generation interceptor capable of speeds exceeding 600 km/h and designed to address increasingly sophisticated aerial threats.
Vigilant Works has recently entered active battlefield testing of Algiz-2 and secured its first commercial agreements outside Ukraine. The company is also developing its proprietary autonomy stack and radar solutions in Ukraine, with investment capital supporting continued technology development and preparations to scale production and operations across NATO-allied countries. The company is a member of Brave1, Ukraine's defense technology coordination platform, and was previously selected for the Brave1 / Ministry of Defence EU4UA program.
"We are excited to support Vigilant Works as they continue developing and scaling their autonomous defense capabilities," said Kyle Asman , Managing Partner at Backswing Ventures. "The evolution of aerial threats is creating an increasingly urgent need for effective counter-UAS solutions. Vigilant Works has the benefit of developing its technology in an environment where these capabilities are being tested against real operational requirements. We believe the team's focus on autonomous interception, radar, and high-speed threats addresses an important and growing need across the defense ecosystem."
"We believe the next leap in counter-UAS will come from rethinking the entire interception chain, much like rocketry did decades ago. Detection, radar, autonomy, and high-speed interception cannot be developed in isolation. We're building them as one integrated system, designed from the ground up to push the boundaries of autonomous air defense," said Daniel Korogodski, CEO & Co-Founder of Vigilant Works.
"Building both the autonomy software and the interceptor platform gives us a unique advantage. We learn directly from Ukraine's best interceptor pilots, turn real-world operational experience into data, and iterate at a pace few can match. We're not just automating today's best pilots, we're building autonomy to outperform them," said Bohdan Boryslavski, CTO & Co-Founder of Vigilant Works.
Vigilant Works is continuing to expand its international footprint while preparing to scale production and operations across allied markets. The company's development efforts are focused on building an integrated autonomous counter-UAS ecosystem capable of addressing the next generation of aerial threats.
For more information, visit https://backswingventures.com/ and https://vgw.systems/ .
About Backswing Ventures
Backswing Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm investing in defense and security technology companies. The firm partners with founders building technologies critical to national security, resilience, and the future of defense.
About Vigilant Works
Vigilant Works is a Ukrainian defense technology company developing autonomous counter-unmanned aerial systems, high-speed interceptor platforms, and radar-based detection technologies. Through its Algiz interceptor platform and proprietary autonomy technologies, the company is building next-generation solutions to address evolving aerial threats and support modern air defense operations.
